title: Futuro simple: predicciones sobre lo que vendrá

sections.content: The simple future (comenzará, tendrán que, explicará) lets a historical text step forward and predict a general pattern -- what revolutionary movements tend to face next -- rather than narrate a specific past event, a useful shift in register just before the reading turns to a concrete case. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El verdadero desafío comenzará después: construir un nuevo Estado capaz de gobernar un país profundamente fracturado.
items.english: The real challenge will begin afterward: building a new state capable of governing a deeply fractured country.

items.spanish: Los movimientos revolucionarios exitosos tendrán que enfrentar preguntas que ninguna consigna previa a la victoria logra responder por sí sola.
items.english: Successful revolutionary movements will have to face questions that no pre-victory slogan manages to answer on its own.

items.spanish: La fase que sigue a una victoria revolucionaria será, con frecuencia, más violenta que la propia lucha por el poder.
items.english: The phase that follows a revolutionary victory will often be more violent than the struggle for power itself.

items.spanish: Esta tensión explicará por qué tantos movimientos terminarán derivando hacia formas de gobierno alejadas de sus ideales fundacionales.
items.english: This tension will explain why so many movements will end up drifting toward forms of government far from their founding ideals.

sections.content: The simple future here is not about a single event on the calendar -- it's a rhetorical move, framing a general historical pattern as something the reader will now watch unfold, which is exactly what the next unit's concrete case study delivers.
